23-22 Floor Area Regulations for R6 Through R12 Districts

In the districts indicated, the maximum #residential# #floor area ratio# shall be as set forth in the following table. Separate maximum #residential# #floor area ratios# are set forth for #zoning lots# containing standard #residences# and #zoning lots# containing #qualifying affordable housing# or #qualifying senior housing#.

MAXIMUM FLOOR AREA RATIO FOR R6-R12 DISTRICTS

[table - see structured `table` field]

1 For #zoning lots#, or portions thereof, located within 100 feet of a #wide street#

2 Outside of #Mandatory Inclusionary Housing areas#, for #zoning lots#, or portions thereof, located within 100 feet of a #wide street#, containing #UAP developments# or #qualifying senior housing#

table.caption: MAXIMUM FLOOR AREA RATIO FOR R6-R12 DISTRICTS
columns: Qualifying affordable housing or qualifying senior housing

footnotes.1: For #zoning lots#, or portions thereof, located within 100 feet of a #wide street#
footnotes.2: Outside of #Mandatory Inclusionary Housing areas#, for #zoning lots#, or portions thereof, located within 100 feet of a #wide street#, containing #UAP developments# or #qualifying senior housing#

notes: Captured as the governing-source candidate for the R6-R12 residential FAR draft rule family.

SUPERSCRIPT PLACEMENT VERIFIED AT THE BYTE LEVEL from the raw HTML, not inferred: row 1 carries R6<sup>1</sup> (the marker is on R6 only, NOT on R6A, R6-1 or R7B); row 5 carries R7-1<sup>1</sup> and R7-2<sup>1</sup>; on the R8 row the markers sit on the VALUES (7.20<sup>1</sup>, 8.64<sup>2</sup>), not on the district label.

CONSEQUENCE - four districts are NOT a flat lookup. R6, R7-1, R7-2 and R8 each appear TWICE in this table with different values: the higher value applies only within 100 feet of a #wide street# (footnote 1), the lower value otherwise. R6 3.00 vs 2.20; R7-1/R7-2 4.00 vs 3.44; R8 7.20 vs 6.02. Footnote 1 says 'or portions thereof', so a single lot can be split between both values and the result is a geometry computation, NOT a table lookup. A rule citing this snapshot MUST NOT return the higher value without a wide-street determination.

#wide street# is defined in ZR 12-10 and is already captured in this repo at docs/research/zr-snapshots/v1/zr-12-10.snapshot.json: 'A wide street is a street that is 75 feet or more in width. A narrow street is a street that is less than 75 feet in width.'

The footnote-2 condition on the R8 qualifying value is COMPOUND - outside a Mandatory Inclusionary Housing area AND within 100 feet of a wide street AND containing UAP developments or qualifying senior housing. None of those three are determined here.

'Qualifying affordable housing' and 'qualifying senior housing' are conditional/eligibility programs (higher FAR). Whether a given lot or development qualifies is a separate legal determination and is NOT decided by this snapshot or by any agent.

CROSS-CHECK: the owner supplied an independent PDF of this section generated by https://zr.planning.nyc.gov on 9/10/2026. All 16 rows, all values, both footnotes and the 12/5/2024 amendment date match this HTML capture exactly. Two independent official channels agree.
Nothing in this record is a Verified zoning determination. Verified requires an M4 published rule with G6 qualified-human legal approval.
